react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity — converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal (FDR 7.80e-13 in RaMP; p = 5.49e-06 in MetaboAnalystR; p = 6.72e-04 in Mummichog). Five driver metabolites span the two major arms of the pathway: the serotonin–melatonin neurochemical branch (L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine–NAD+ branch (L-tryptophan → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid → NAD+). RaMP additionally identifies the WikiPathways IDO metabolic pathway (FDR 3.96e-09) and NAD+ biosynthetic pathways from tryptophan (FDR 9.61e-09), while Reactome's Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931, FDR 9.11e-09) captures the neurochemical downstream products. The five-core hit pattern across all three methods is not driven by a single outlier: each of the five metabolites resolves to a unique InChIKey first-block (reconcile_inchikey, 8 clusters, 0 conflicts), confirming no namespace artefact. The peripheral metabolites — O-phosphoethanolamine, 3-methyladenine, and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid — appear only as isolated single-hit entries in Mummichog or marginally in MetaboAnalystR (hsa00760, p = 0.0553) and do not replicate across paradigms. The biological story is one of coordinated tryptophan catabolism: the treatment group shows differential abundance across both the neuroactive serotonin–melatonin axis and the immunomodulatory kynurenine–quinolinic acid axis, suggesting a perturbation that simultaneously affects serotonergic signalling and NAD+ precursor flux.
